pageCache.text:
Halcyon London International School
An innovative curriculum that encourages academic curiosity. Classrooms where challenging questions deepen understanding. Students welcomed for who they are.
This is how we draw out the unique potential of each student. This is Halcyon London International School. You are welcome here.
Halcyon is a leading International Baccalaureate school for students aged 11 to 18 – the only not-for-profit IB school in London. Our mission is to provide an exceptional education that draws out the unique potential of each student. At Halcyon, enquiring minds flourish when paired with our innovative approach to the IB curriculum. Students collaborate with teachers and their peers, achieving ambitious academic goals and confidently meeting high levels of personal growth. Halcyon delivers a unique, research-driven approach to wellbeing. Students feel valued, confident and secure. We embed cutting-edge technology into learning. Our students are supremely well-prepared for the digital revolution of today and tomorrow. Visit us in Marylebone, at the beating heart of central London. We pioneer education.
At Halcyon, we believe that collaboration sparks creativity. We are small-by-design, allowing for close-knit connections among teachers and students alike. Teachers collaborate closely in planning and delivering lessons, ensuring a cohesive and integrated educational experience. Students are encouraged to share ideas, challenge assumptions, and learn from one another, celebrating the diversity of perspectives within our classrooms. Innovation is at the heart of our teaching, with cutting-edge technology integrated into our curriculum. With a dedicated Digital Learning Coach on staff, we create bespoke virtual environments and utilise advanced tools like Canva and AI platforms such as DALL-E, preparing students for a digital future.
Our expert teachers harness the interdisciplinary potential of the IB, enabling students to understand, articulate and interrogate the often complex and interconnected nature of knowledge. Our students develop a deep comprehension of what they’ve learned, laying robust foundations for successful and fulfilling futures.
IB Middle Years Programme
IB Diploma Programme
Wellbeing is fundamental to unlocking each student's unique potential. We create an environment where students feel safe to flourish as individuals, and they feel valued when they do. This is why our students can flourish academically. Our research-driven approach to wellbeing powers our growth-focused environment, built around shared values, not rules, mirroring top university and professional environments. Our Student Wellbeing Lead, a qualified restorative practitioner, sits on the Senior Leadership Team, ensuring that wellbeing is prioritised at the highest level. We co-create additional learning opportunities with our students, encouraging them to take responsibility for developing their broader interests. We provide personalised, research-informed mentoring, to every student, every week, every grade. This is why our students develop autonomy, resilience and their own sense of self. This is a character building education fit for the realities of the 21st century.
Our innovative approach to the International Baccalaureate (IB) develops the critical thinking, interdisciplinary awareness and collaborative skills required for success at the world’s most prestigious universities. Our personalised university and careers counselling, and programme of support, provide students with the tools to choose the best path for their future fulfilment. Connected to university admissions offices around the world, our University and Careers Counselling Director brings specialist knowledge to Halcyon that creates college- and career-ready global citizens. Benefitting from a range of one-to-one and grade-level university counselling services, each learner is guided to make decisions and develop skills that unlock opportunities in higher education. Our University and Careers Counselling Director is available to everyone in Halcyon’s small community, delivering individualised, comprehensive support to each student and their family.
University and Careers Counselling
Leavers' Destinations
At Halcyon, we look holistically at prospective students, considering how well they will suit the demands of, and opportunities presented by, the International Baccalaureate. Our students actively engage with our innovative curriculum, thoughtfully designed to encourage academic curiosity. They work in classrooms where they ask, and are asked, challenging questions, to deepen their understanding. They enrich our community's cultural and academic knowledge, by bringing in their unique perspectives and experiences.
Read all about how our community flourishes in our environment of educational innovation, collaborative thinking and research-driven approach to wellbeing.
Community is a foundational value for us. Successful communities learn and create together, supported by a culture of shared values. At Halcyon, we are committed to creating an inclusive community that appreciates and respects each person. Each month we spotlight a member of our community, discovering the person behind the role.
Accreditations
We are proud to hold a diverse range of accreditations that reflect our commitment to excellence in education. They highlight our commitment to rigorous academic standards and the provision of a high-quality learning environment that draws out the unique potential of each student. These accreditations are a testament to our dedication to our values of innovation, collaboration and community.
Halcyon London International School is a leading International Baccalaureate School in Marylebone, central London. Our mission is to provide an exceptional education that draws out the unique potential of each student. Our values are innovation, collaboration and community. We operate on a not-for-profit model, meaning our income is reinvested in our educational provision and not paid out to shareholders.

pageCache.pageTitle: Director's Welcome - Halcyon London International School
pageCache.text:
Director's Welcome
We are pleased to announce that Jeff Lippman has accepted the offer of Halcyon Director, starting at the beginning of the 2025/26 school year
In his 30 years in education, Jeff has worked in international schools in Brazil, Spain, France and the US, beginning by teaching history and later moving into leadership roles. Jeff prides himself on being a life-long learner. He speaks Portuguese fluently and Spanish and French to a high level of proficiency, as well as his native English.
"I feel so honoured to have the chance to join the Halcyon community and serve as your next director. As soon as I arrived on campus, it became readily apparent to me that Halcyon is a place that lives its values every day by creating a joyful learning environment where students have a voice.
I was struck by the consistency of what I heard from all stakeholders: the pride in the culture that has been built, the desire to continue innovating, and a deep commitment to inclusion and belonging.
As I walked the hallways with my student guide, I asked him what he likes best about Halcyon. Without hesitation, he said, “It's the community. Everyone cares for each other here.” In my cover letter I wrote: “More than just a school, I am seeking to be part of a warm and vibrant community that is bound together by common values.” I feel so fortunate to have found just that in Halcyon."

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Mission - Halcyon London International School
pageCache.text:
Our Mission
To provide an exceptional education that draws out the unique potential of each student. Halcyon is a leading International Baccalaureate school for students aged 11 to 18 – the only not-for-profit IB school in London.
Collaboration is at the core of our community of life-long learners. Learning together we build different perspectives as we understand ourselves in relation to others. This experience allows each of us to navigate the world successfully and shape who we want to be.
We intentionally create an environment that develops and encourages collaborative learning and teaching through the promotion of trust, mutual respect, shared values and leadership.
Collaboration is present in our leadership approach, our learning spaces, our staff workshops, our coaching dialogue, and through the passion of student initiative and engagement. Collaborative practice is supported by our pioneering wellbeing programme and our emphasis on restorative practice and fostering ownership, agency, voice, and belonging.
Halcyon understands that successful communities learn and create together, supported by a culture of shared values. We are committed to creating an inclusive community that appreciates and respects each person.
All are welcomed to contribute and develop a sense of agency and ownership of the school and its mission. Just as we wish all students to fulfil their unique potential, we actively nurture the same opportunities for growth for everyone in our community. We also commit to participating in the wider community through service-learning and engaging constructively with wider social challenges.
The Halcyon community emboldens and supports every learner to be an explorer, a risk-taker and a creative problem-solver. We embrace challenging questions and seek out purposeful, research-led answers.
To build this creative, curious and questioning culture, Halcyon’s IB curriculum is designed to promote self-directed learning and critical thinking.
Our work is enriched by pioneering digital resources, fully integrated into our school practice.
Our Mission and the International Baccalaureate
Through its mission, the International Baccalaureate aims to develop inquiring, knowledgeable and caring young people who help to create a better and more peaceful world through intercultural understanding and respect.
To this end the organisation works with schools, governments and international organisations to develop challenging programmes of international education and rigorous assessment. These programmes encourage students across the world to become active, compassionate and lifelong learners who understand that other people, with their differences, can also be right.
Through its mission, Halcyon is committed to delivering an exceptional International Baccalaureate education – a curriculum that equips its students with the skills to succeed in a complex, ever-changing world.
International Baccalaureate Organisation

pageCache.pageTitle: Fundamental British Values - Halcyon London International School
pageCache.text:
Fundamental British Values
Through our Personal, Social, Health, and Economic Education (PSHEE) programme, spiritual, moral, social and cultural (SMSC) development is a mandatory teaching requirement in all schools in England.
SMSC education is also the vehicle through which we teach Fundamental British Values (FBV). One might also conceive of this as citizenship education. A key part of the IB mission is that students strive to be ‘active, compassionate and lifelong learners […] who help to create a better and more peaceful world through intercultural understanding and respect’.
Spiritual, moral, social and cultural development
Definition of Fundamental British Values
Halcyon uses London as a classroom; we have immediate access to museums, galleries, universities, theatres, global businesses, creative industries and so much more. We take students to workshops and lectures, exhibitions and plays, and to experience the rich world of work across the city.
We also have designated Discovery Days, when students will learn about specific areas of the city’s history or culture, or will be learning with experts in a particular field. For example, this year our Grade 10 students explored the work of the Royal Courts of Justice, while Grade 6 enjoyed some hands-on science at The Royal Botanical Gardens in Kew.
Discovery Days, and our many learning excursions across the city, allow students to make better connections with the wider community and build a better understanding of the city’s identity and culture.
Luna, Grade 6 student reflection
"We went to Kew Gardens with a brilliant tour guide who taught us how to measure different aspects of ecosystems like soil, temperature, moisture and humidity. We compared the outside conditions with the Palm House, a giant greenhouse containing a tropical rainforest. We learnt about plants with cancer-fighting properties, which was fascinating. We also saw other plants used to cure diseases. As we wandered around taking photographs, we discovered a bridge over a pond with a massive fish and impressively large lily pads. The pathways were lined with hanging vines that kept hitting our faces, and the humidity created water droplets everywhere. it was really hot and humid! "We then explored another glasshouse containing different biomes, including desert, temperate rainforest, tropical ferns and rainforest sections. Having just studied carnivorous plants in science, we were excited to spot pitcher plants in the desert section. "Instead of just looking things up online, we got to experience everything in person. Back at school, we created a Venn diagram comparing the tropical rainforest and urban ecosystem, noting the significant differences in temperature and soil moisture levels between the two environments."
Charlie, Grade 10 student reflection
“We went to both the Old Bailey and the Royal Courts of Justice. At the Old Bailey we had the opportunity to watch a case in process - a man charged with murder! There was palpable tension in the line of people queuing to get into the court; there were some high profile cases in process at the time.
“It was interesting to see the jury in real life and to see the real workings of the criminal justice system. I didn't know that the barristers still wore those white wigs. I learned that the whiter the wig the less experience a barrister has. I was also told that some will deliberately stain their wigs with tea to make them look older!
“The purpose of the day was to learn about the justice system and to see this is real life through court proceedings. It was also interesting to learn about the cost of justice and how the process of legal aid functions for those who cannot afford legal advice. We learned that as a result of the pandemic, and a limited budget,, the legal system is under great strain. This has many negative impacts, especially for those who require legal aid.”

Inspections and Accreditations
Choosing a school is an act of trust. At Halcyon, we believe that trust should be earned — and independently verified. On this page you'll find our full inspection history, our accreditations and what independent reviewers say about us, presented openly and in full. We invite you to read every word.
All Independent School Standards met — ISI, October 2024
Ofsted Outstanding — 2020 and 2017
Authorised IB World School — MYP & DP
NEASC accredited — ACE Learning protocol
Independently reviewed by The Good Schools Guide
Our latest inspection:
ISI, October 2024
Halcyon is inspected by the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI), the body appointed by the Department for Education to inspect association independent schools in England. In October 2024, ISI conducted a routine inspection of Halcyon and found that the school meets all of the statutory Independent School Standards — across leadership and governance, quality of education, and pupils' physical and mental health and emotional wellbeing.
Inspectors recognised the strength of teaching at Halcyon, noting that teachers use secure subject knowledge to deliver ambitious content in line with the IB's philosophy of students building knowledge through research. They highlighted the school's detailed, well-considered curriculum, enriched by cultural visits across central London, and found that our safeguarding arrangements effectively promote students' wellbeing, with help given quickly when students need it.
Pupils come from culturally rich and nationally diverse backgrounds. Many have been previously educated overseas. Leaders have established an ethos of inclusivity in which pupils with different backgrounds, faiths and gender preference feel comfortable and valued. As a result, pupils are self-confident and positive about difference.
Independent schools inspectorate report
Ofsted: Outstanding, twice over
Before joining the Independent Schools Association, Halcyon was inspected directly by Ofsted. In our two most recent Ofsted inspections, March 2020, and April 2017. Halcyon was rated Outstanding, the highest judgement available.
In 2020, inspectors observed that teachers at Halcyon are passionate about their subjects, with strong subject knowledge running through a curriculum that connects concepts across disciplines. They described students whose quality of work is excellent respectful, self-confident, independent and quietly determined.
March 2020 — Outstanding
A standard inspection rating Halcyon Outstanding in all categories.
Read the full report
April 2017 - Outstanding
Halcyon's first Outstanding rating, four years after opening.
Read the full report
The Good Schools Guide
The Good Schools Guide is the UK's most trusted independent guide to schools. Schools cannot pay to be included; reviews are researched through school visits and conversations with students, parents and staff, and written entirely independently.
"In general, students are supportive of each other. ‘There’s a culture of excellence, but not competition. We’re all here to learn with each other."
Read the full review
NEASC: a pioneer of the ACE Learning protocol
Halcyon is accredited by the New England Association of Schools and Colleges (NEASC), one of the world's most respected school accreditation bodies, founded in 1885 and trusted by leading international schools across more than 80 countries.
What sets Halcyon's accreditation apart is how we earned it. Halcyon was one of the first schools in the world to be accredited through NEASC's ACE Learning protocol — a deliberately demanding model that moved beyond the traditional checklist approach to school evaluation. Rather than asking whether a school's paperwork is in order, ACE Learning asks a harder question: what impact is this school actually having on its learners?
The ACE protocol evaluates a school as a living learning ecosystem, examining the alignment between what a school says it values and what students actually experience, day to day. It is a growth model — focused on transformation, not box-ticking — and it requires sustained self-study, external peer review by experienced international educators, and evidence of genuine learning impact.
For prospective families, NEASC accreditation offers two practical assurances. First, that Halcyon's educational quality has been examined against a rigorous international standard, independent of the UK inspection framework — a second, separate lens on the school. Second, that a Halcyon education is internationally portable: NEASC accreditation is recognised by universities and schools worldwide, and qualifying Halcyon students receive an accredited US high school diploma alongside their IB qualifications — valuable for families whose futures may span more than one country.
Additional Accredidations
We are proud to hold a diverse range of accreditations that reflect our commitment to excellence in education. They highlight our commitment to rigorous academic standards and the provision of a high-quality learning environment that draws out the unique potential of each student. These accreditations are a testament to our dedication to our values of innovation, collaboration and community.
Eco-Schools accreditation acknowledges and celebrates the ecological achievements of young people. It that, as a community, we are forward-thinking and promote youth-led environmental education and action.
This accredited membership marks a significant milestone in our commitment to educational excellence and innovation. ISA membership provides exciting opportunities to work with, learn from and inspire schools from across the international and independent schools sectors. As an active member of the ISA, we will continue to foster educational innovation; innovation driven by our collaborative practice and underpinned by our unwavering commitment to community values. Accredited membership enables us to further the values of the International Baccalaureate Organisations mission: to develop inquiring, knowledgeable and caring young people who help to create a better and more peaceful world through intercultural understanding and respect.
Halcyon was one of the first schools to go through NEASC's ACE accreditation protocol. This accreditation moved from the 19th century tick box approach of measuring educational excellence to a growth model, focusing on transforming rather than improving schools; and on the impact of our education on students - rather than commodifying those students in the guise of their outcomes.
The Good Schools Guide makes annual visits to the best schools, so they can provide impartial, straight-talking and thoroughly researched reviews for parents.
Council of British International Schools membership is open to British international schools of global quality. All member schools must meet their rigorous quality assurance standards to demonstrate their commitment to their pupils and school community.
Google Reference Schools are recognised by Google for their outstanding use of technology to drive positive learning outcomes. Each has agreed to host visitors on-site, share advice, tips, and best practices, host events, and more.
Apple Regional Training Centres are a community of educators and institutions, who provide online and face to face training, to build the skills and confidence of educators in using Apple technology inside and outside the classroom.
Gender Action exists to address gender imbalances on a structural level within education. As a recognised supporter, we commit to a whole-school approach to transforming our school environment, so that students' genders do not act as a limit on their interests, capabilities or ambitions.
The Edtech 50 is a landmark publication – it inspires and is used as a reference point by policy makers, government and educators. As an EdTech 50 school, we are recognised as one of the best schools in the country for integrating EdTech and harnessing its capabilities to enhance students' ability to access and understand the curriculum.
This accreditation recognises our delivery of a solely International Baccalaureate curriculum. It makes us part of a community of over 5,000 schools globally, that deliver IB programmes to students to help create a better and more peaceful world through cultural understanding and respect.
Yes. Halcyon was rated Outstanding by Ofsted in both of its two most recent Ofsted inspections, in March 2020 and April 2017. Since joining the Independent Schools Association, Halcyon's statutory inspections are carried out by the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) rather than Ofsted, which is standard practice for association independent schools in England.
Halcyon's most recent inspection, carried out by the Independent Schools Inspectorate in October 2024, found that the school meets all of the statutory Independent School Standards. Inspectors highlighted the strength of teaching, the well-designed curriculum enriched by London's cultural opportunities, and safeguarding arrangements that effectively promote student wellbeing. The full report is available to download on this page.
Both inspect schools in England against the same statutory Independent School Standards. Ofsted inspects state schools and non-association independent schools, while the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) is appointed by the Department for Education to inspect independent schools that belong to associations within the Independent Schools Council. As a member of the Independent Schools Association, Halcyon is inspected by ISI.
Yes. Halcyon is an authorised IB World School, delivering both the IB Middle Years Programme (ages 11–16) and the IB Diploma Programme (ages 16–18). Halcyon is the only not-for-profit IB school in London.
NEASC (the New England Association of Schools and Colleges) is one of the world's most established school accreditation bodies, and Halcyon is accredited through its ACE Learning protocol — a rigorous, growth-focused model that evaluates the real impact a school has on its learners. Halcyon was one of the first schools in the world to complete this protocol. For families, NEASC accreditation provides an internationally recognised assurance of quality, independent of UK inspection, and means qualifying students receive an accredited US high school diploma alongside their IB qualifications.
The Good Schools Guide, which reviews schools independently and does not accept payment for inclusion, describes Halcyon as a friendly, happy, small school devoted to delivering the IB in the best possible way, where students are listened to and supported to strive and thrive.
Independent schools in England are inspected on a routine cycle, typically around every three years, with additional visits possible at any time. Halcyon's most recent routine inspection took place in October 2024. We publish every inspection report in full on this page.
All of Halcyon's inspection reports are available to download on this page, including the 2024 ISI report and the 2020 and 2017 Ofsted reports. They are also published on the official ISI (isi.net) and Ofsted (reports.ofsted.gov.uk) websites.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our History - Halcyon London International School
pageCache.text:
Our History
In 2012, four visionary parents set out to build a pioneering educational community.
Amidst the increasing marketisation of both state and independent schools, they perceived a growing trend: education was being treated as a business rather than a platform to serve the academic and developmental needs of young people. Determined to challenge this trend, they founded Halcyon, a not-for-profit international school, with community and innovation at its heart. In 2013, we opened our doors, and our founders’ vision became a reality.
Halcyon’s story is one of innovation, collaboration, and community.
This pioneering approach attracted like-minded individuals who believed in pursuing what was right, not what was fashionable. With their combined experience in international education, they chose the International Baccalaureate (IB) as the cornerstone of our curriculum, recognising its unique ability to foster both academic and personal development in the quest for a better and more peaceful world.
The founders understood that, like any field or industry, innovation was crucial. Our expert teachers leveraged the IB curriculum as a springboard for this innovation: integrating cutting-edge technology to enhance our students’ ingenuity and capabilities; pursuing a student-centred ‘behaviour’ policy based on values rather than rules. This policy built the capacity of both staff and students to strengthen and grow from mistakes, fostering a community in which everyone felt safe, happy, and valued. In which everyone could prosper.
Our founders' vision was clear from the start: to create an institution where fees were reinvested into the school community rather than distributed to shareholders; invested in developing and maintaining an exceptional education, dedicated to drawing out the unique potential of each student.
One decade on, Halcyon remains true to its founding principles. The school continues to nurture an environment where everyone feels secure and appreciated, thanks to its value-driven approach and commitment to innovation. As we step into the next decade, Halcyon has formed a dedicated Innovation Team focused on exploring the potentials of AI, service, and international mindedness. This team continues to view education as a means to serve the academic and developmental needs of young people, drawing out their unique potential, ready to build a better and more peaceful world.

Successful communities learn and create together, supported by a culture of shared values. At Halcyon, we are committed to creating an inclusive community that appreciates and respects each person.
Just as we wish all students to fulfil their unique potential, we actively nurture the same opportunities for growth for everyone in our community.
With a student body from 6 continents, representing 36 nationalities, a staff body of over 46 different nationalities and alumni in universities and careers worldwide, Halcyon's small community has large reach.

University and Careers Counselling
Connected to university admissions offices around the world, our University and Careers Counselling Director brings specialist knowledge to Halcyon that creates college and career-ready global citizens.
Benefitting from a range of one-to-one and grade-level university counselling services, each learner is guided to make decisions and develop skills that unlock opportunities in higher education. pageCache.pageTitle: Dr Saba Lodhi, Teacher of Chemistry | Posts Detail
pageCache.text:
Dr Saba Lodhi, Teacher of Chemistry
Dr Saba Lodhi is an environmental activist, science researcher, and our very own IB chemistry teacher.
Saba has a gallery of international experiences, from working at a charity school in Milan, to teaching chemistry and kickstarting The Duke of Edinburgh’s International Award programme while in South East Asia, then later teaching and leading Women in STEM movements across Berlin.
In every destination, Saba has transcended the classroom, mobilising environmental action and strengthening the cultural fibre of women in science.
She says, “The world needs a balance in how decisions are made about us. That will come with more representation of women.”
IB Chemistry Teacher Coordinates Women in STEM Assembly
Saba works collaboratively with both staff and students, engaging in real world issues. Her role in the Eco Committee means she is often working on a community initiative, whether it’s co-ordinating the recent Women in STEM assembly at Halcyon, or assisting students with the sustainability pop-up show.
Saba is quick to point out that these events are only possible because of students’ and colleagues’ willingness to work together. “At Halcyon, what is unique is the warm friendly community of staff, teachers and students.”
A Day In The Life Of an IB Chemistry Teacher
A day in the life of Saba is most often spent teaching in the lab, where she takes a shared learning approach to Science and IB Chemistry, buoyed by the diversity of thoughts and expressions of students at Halcyon.
“The way learning is done here, students are able to show their thinking. You can see the tactility of their learning, they can make a note on the table next to them, or collaborate freely with another student. What excites me the most is seeing how they connect with the lesson.”
“I feel special in chemistry, my students have a passion to master what they are learning. They often bring connections to the learning from other lessons – whether it be languages or art – which makes it a fun and authentic application to chemistry in real life.”
The Importance Of Sustainability
When Saba is not in the lab or campaigning for women in science, she is sewing her own clothes, upcycling recycled materials and turning them into beautiful garments.
“I try to wear something I've made every day and abstain from buying something new. The creative aspect of sewing and making helps me unwind and gives clarity to my teaching work, it allows me to pattern my thoughts about how I might approach a lesson.”
When asked about her favourite memories at Halcyon, Saba laughs: “there are too many memories” before sharing experiences of outdoor learning days, such as the Grade 7 Drama in the Woods trip, where she worked with students to build shelters in nature.
Saba often describes Halcyon as a “family”- noting how well connected the staff team are from all departments are and how collaboration opportunities occur naturally.
“We are a family school which makes it different from going to an ordinary school and simply doing your work. We are part of one big community, we are a family with a common goal. We all hold on to that as we grow.”

pageCache.pageTitle: Pilar Delgado, IB DP & MYP Spanish Teacher | Posts Detail
pageCache.text:
Pilar Delgado, IB DP & MYP Spanish Teacher
As an international school, many of our staff and students are multilingual, with a variety of languages often spoken and shared in the classroom. Language is treasured, both in our social world, but also in our view of academic success.
Halcyon’s offered foreign languages are English, Spanish, Mandarin and French – but we also offer the Mother Tongue Programme – which means students can request to learn their native language, and we will find a teacher to deliver them.
But, our foreign languages programme extends past learning words and phrases, it offers different perspectives and frames, and supports new relationships, which can last forever.
The importance of developing relationships in language teaching
Perhaps, there is no better model than our Spanish IB teacher, Pilar Delgado Suarez, who shares her love for language with both students and staff everyday.
Pilar’s teaching style is naturally engaging, inspiring strong relationships with students.
She says part of teaching is about having fun and having a strong link to the target culture and real world, regularly exchanging quips and jokes in Spanish as a way of connecting students with the language as local Spanish people do. “I love idiomatic expressions; the kids are crazy about them.” She laughs. “For example, I often ask in Spanish: How are you feeling? Happy as a clam? Which translates as: feliz como una perdiz.”
A rigorous programme of language acquisition
But the programme is rigorous. MYP students usually start by learning the basics such as the alphabet, before moving onto tenses, learning about the Spanish environment, then advancing into debating global issues and current events in the Hispanic world.
“At the end when they follow your guidance, they can’t believe they have achieved the ability to discuss things like immigration in a second language. It’s always special to see how students grow.”
Pilar has over fifteen years of experience teaching, moderating, and examining the IB Programme.
“I always wanted to be a teacher and I love being an IB teacher; I love the freedom it offers. The opportunity of being at a new school, but having a solid understanding of the IB was really important. I really enjoy teaching outside the classroom, going to museums, galleries, and on trips to Spain.”
London as a classroom
Pilar designs her own educational environment, which extends beyond the classroom and into the city. “Halcyon has so many opportunities for a teacher. Being a part of central London has opened my eyes to being a Spanish teacher. An educational opportunity could be in the form of a letter to the mayor, a walk around Portobello Road, a lecture in Kings’ College; there is so much learning to be had on our doorstep.”
Pilar draws from a wide range of resources to make learning language feel tangible and purposeful, such as fulfilling a student's wish to see a dance show or inviting a local artist to help with a visual arts project in Spanish.
It’s these real-world examples that allow students to gain a deeper perspective of the language they are learning. Take Spanish Immersion Day last year, for example, where Pilar invited her students to be curators in a Spanish Art Exhibition, learn about the cultural conventions of Spanish artefacts, then later bond over Spanish cuisine, trying their hand at ordering meals in a restaurant setting.
“It was a lovely time. It’s important to present their work outside of their classroom. Both the gallery and the restaurant we visited were really impressed by the students, and it was a meaningful way of practising our language in a real tangible context with a different type of audience”
Pilar says her favourite part of teaching at Halcyon is the people. “Halcyon has a real sense of community and a caring atmosphere to work in. Students and teachers have an opportunity to be vulnerable. It’s okay to say you are not okay, everyone is understanding of your situation.”
In terms of her favourite spots in the city, Pilar enjoys visiting the Victoria and Albert Museum, swimming in the pool, drinking coffee and eating croquetas. “I love going to exhibitions and shows. The Royal Opera House is my happy place. I love taking kids to exhibitions and instilling this passion of mine in them. I love live music and street photography. I love everything about the arts.”

At Halcyon, we are committed to nurturing our students' passions.

pageCache.pageTitle: Board of Trustees - Halcyon London International School
pageCache.text:
Board of Trustees
Early on in the discussions that were to become Halcyon, co-founders Achim, Julie, Pamela and I were inspired by a number of overlapping visions of why we needed to create Halcyon. As we reflect on our first ten years, I’d like to share with you what led me on this journey which, frankly, has become a life-defining achievement for me. I hope it has been an equally life-affirming experience for those who have become involved with Halcyon; as student, staff, parent or otherwise.
Thinking back on the early conversations, we were committed to creating an innovative, student-centred learning environment. One based on current research and modern thinking. We read books and articles, attended talks and conferences, visited other schools and were attracted to the educators who spoke of making education more relevant and innovative, such as Sugata Mitra and Sir Ken Robinson. Both of these educational leaders spoke endlessly about how student-centred learning allows students to take ownership and raises their level of engagement. That spoke to us!
Education seemed to be one of the very few sectors whose approach had barely changed in decades. Yet we all expect and want the “latest” thinking when it comes to healthcare, engineering and more. Why did society seem to accept yesteryear for education - which should be our investment in the future - when the rest of the world constantly evolves?

Our Facilities
From versatile classrooms equipped with Apple TVs and whiteboard tables, to science and design laboratories with cutting-edge equipment, our campus supports a diverse range of academic and extracurricular activities.
We take great pride in providing our students, staff, and community with in-house facilities that foster an enriching and conducive learning environment, supplemented by facilities in our local community of Marylebone and central London.
Our wonderful Learning Coach works with students both within class and outside interventions in her dedicated office to support mild to moderate learning needs, providing students with scaffolds, strategies and accommodations. She also leads staff development workshops regularly to enhance inclusive and accessible practice throughout the school.
More on Additional Educational Needs
Our vibrant studio space offers diverse media and materials, fostering creativity as students build their course process portfolios in an inspiring space. We display student artwork throughout the building, infusing our wider environment with the creativity, joy and individuality of the studio.
Our state-of-the-art design laboratory is a hub of creativity, equipped with a 3D printer, laser cutter, and a workshop table. Here, students immerse themselves in a range of skills from traditional woodworking and jewellery making to cutting-edge graphic design. Past projects have included coding interactive games and crafting energising 'brain-boosting' smoothies to fuel their learning.
Diploma Programme students have their own dedicated study space, both a social hub and a place to collaborate and revise. Our Diploma Coordinator, University and Careers Counselling Director and Wellbeing Lead are often based here, giving immediate access for students whenever they need support.
Our school library is a vibrant hub for learning and exploration. During school hours, students can enjoy our cosy onsite library, perfect for browsing and reading.
Where our library truly excels is our extensive online catalogue, accessible 24/7 from anywhere in the world. Additionally, every student receives membership to the Westminster Library, granting them both online and in-person access to a vast collection of books and academic journals, ideal for their research and academic pursuits.
Digital Library Login as guest to view
IB learners acquire the skills and knowledge to investigate problems in real-world contexts, and learning in central London enriches every student’s school experience. The city’s world-class universities, theatres, museums, galleries and exhibitions provide opportunities for each child to take their learning from our campus to every corner of our vibrant city. Our students could be beach combing on the Thames to explore the past, discovering the history of natural science in South Kensington’s museums, or enhancing their language skills by enjoying Mandarin or Spanish productions in London’s best theatres.
Students have access to a wide range of instruments in school, for use in lessons as well as through our peripatetic classes. Students follow a varied digital curriculum including learning how to use Logic, the industry-standard music production software. Students can also take part in our school band or perform in our annual music showcase.
As well as our own hall space, used for indoor activities such as table tennis, dance and fitness, we make use of various nearby leisure centres and facilities, such as Paddington Recreation Ground and Hyde Park, to offer a range of sports from football, basketball and volleyball to dance, running and kickboxing.
Our Sports Programme
We use technology intentionally and transformatively. Our utilisation of digital tools is targeted, curriculum-oriented and research-led, and drives a thoughtful, forward-looking and reflective approach to pedagogy across our team, with our dedicated Digital Learning Coach supporting our community to remain innovative, responsible and reflective in our approach to technology.
All students work from an iPad or a laptop. Lessons and student work are uploaded to Google Classroom, which can be accessed by parents. Students benefit from our institutional subscriptions to a variety of educational technologies, including Google for Education and Canva for Education.

pageCache.pageTitle: UN Biodiversity Day Q&A with Martyn Steiner (Teacher of Science) | Posts Detail
pageCache.text:
UN Biodiversity Day Q&A with Martyn Steiner (Teacher of Science)
At Halcyon, we pride ourselves on connecting students with real-world issues. We elevate subjects like science beyond traditional worksheet lab experiments, engaging students with global challenges such as climate change and biodiversity loss.
For United Nations Biodiversity Day, we spoke with Halcyon IB Science Teacher, Mr Steiner, who provides students with the tools to identify and explore the living world around them—even the humble whitlowgrass between cobblestones!
Can you speak about the postgraduate course you are currently doing on ecological survey techniques? When did you start this field of study? And how has it strengthened/deepened your teaching of science?
Halcyon have supported me to take the course over two years through the University of Oxford's Department for Continuing Education. It has enhanced my subject knowledge of specific techniques I was less familiar with, such as fish surveying, but also created space for me to have innovative ideas about practical research projects to involve students in.
How can science educators and schools engage with real world issues like biodiversity and species loss?
One of the biggest challenges we face is that biodiversity loss can feel quite removed from students day-to-day experience of life in the city. At the same time, people tend to perceive whatever they grew up with as normal and so the biodiversity loss we have already experienced becomes the baseline for the next generation. For that reason, I think it's hugely important that we show students how biodiversity loss is relevant to their own lives, how much has been lost already and how they can be empowered to address it.
What are some projects you have done, or currently doing, which covers the issue of biodiversity here at Halcyon?
For my final research project for my course I'm comparing plant biodiversity in mews (small side streets) with either cobbled or tarmacked surfaces - it is really incredible how much life reveals itself between the cracks when you stop to look. I have engaged my students as citizen scientists in this project - some have just learned research techniques by collecting data (techniques that can be used for their own coursework) and others have been actively involved in co-planning the methods. I really loved the opportunity to show my grade 10 class that science investigations are more than just blindly following a recipe for mixing chemicals - they are a creative endeavour that require real world problem-solving.
How does Halcyon enable creative, real-world applications of science to connect with biodiversity?
A great feature of MYP science is that the students have to explain and evaluate the use of science, showing that they understand that scientific solutions have societal consequences. Some of my students have been asked to take what they have learned from the mews project and to use it to write to a local politician with advice about action that should be taken to support biodiversity - I hope that they will be able to send these out and take service as engaged members of their local community.
Conversations on biodiversity in cities are often centred around parks or obvious ‘green spaces’ – but why is it important to examine neglected areas like mews?
Those obvious green spaces are hugely important and we need more of them, but they can allow for a sense that nature exists 'out there' and that we live our normal lives divorced from the natural world. Engaging with nature closer to home can help blur those boundaries. I also love that we're looking at unnoticed species - while common whitlowgrass may lack the charisma of a leaping dolphin it still has its own important role to play in an ecosystem. And as the Potawatomi botanist Robin Wall Kimmerer observes, to form a relationship with someone you must first get to know their name!
What have been some of your memorable discoveries when teaching the topic of biodiversity?
I think one of the most striking things for me is just how much life still clings on even on a busy road in central London. I encourage everyone to take a five minute walk closely looking at the ground and just count how many plant species you see!

IB Diploma Results
We are immensely proud to celebrate the achievements of our Class of 2025 International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme (IBDP) students.
The first International Baccalaureate Diploma examinations were held in 1971, for 601 students in 12 schools; last year, in 2024, there were 21,806 students in 1427 schools in 125 countries. Our IB graduates join a thriving dynamic, aspirational, international community, with those special IB skills that allow them to make a difference in the world.
We believe that the IB Diploma is the best university-entrance examination in the world, and it gives our students access to the very best universities and programmes. Each year our students excel, and our Class of 2025 joins this proud tradition of academic excellence, personal and civic leadership, and personal growth. As a community, we are so pleased to celebrate together the achievements of the Class of 2025, and we wish them the very best as they embark on new adventures and extraordinary journeys all around the world.
Congratulations to each and every one of our wonderful graduates.
We are so proud of our class of 2025 and the results they achieved through their own hard work and their collaborative teamwork. What stands out from this class though is more than just the numbers and grades - it is the eloquent TOK essay, the ethereal art work, the authentic science discovery, the original music composition and the intentions to make a difference. Well done to the Class of 2025!
- Ms Lori Fritz, IBDP Coordinator

Our students' diverse talents and passions are reflected in their chosen university destinations and courses.
